transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I feel like nobody in my family is really listening to me about what’s been going on. It’s my husband’s sister—she’s been working this family business in a way that, to me, is very clear. She’s trying to get control of the money, and little by little push me out of decisions that I should have a say in.

People keep trying to smooth it over, you know, like, “Oh, that’s just how she is,” or “Don’t worry about it,” but I know what I’ve been seeing. This hasn’t been just a bad week or me misunderstanding one conversation. It’s been going on for more than a year now, and after a while you start putting the pieces together. I came here because I’m tired of being made to feel like I’m imagining it when I know what’s happening.
Can you tell me more about what makes you believe your husband’s sister is trying to take control of the family business and push you out of decisions?

It’s not just one thing, that’s what I keep trying to explain to everybody. If it was one conversation or one bad look, I could let it go. But it’s been little things, over and over, for more than a year now, and they all point the same direction.

She gets herself in the middle of everything with the business, especially when it comes to the money. She’ll talk to people before I even know there was something being discussed, and then by the time it gets back to me, it’s like the decision is already half-made. And if I say, “Wait, why wasn’t I included?” then everyone acts like I’m making a problem where there isn’t one.

That’s what bothers me. They smooth it over. My husband will say, “She didn’t mean it that way,” or, “You’re reading too much into it,” but I’m not. I know what I’m seeing. She’s trying to get control, little by little, and push me out so I don’t have a say. Maybe she thinks if she does it slowly enough nobody will notice, but I noticed. I’ve been watching it happen.
Can you tell me if you have ever felt certain about something that others later told you wasn’t true, even though you were sure at the time?

Yes, I mean… that’s exactly what’s been happening with this whole thing. People keep telling me I’m wrong about his sister, or that I’m taking it the wrong way, or that there’s some innocent explanation for it. But I know what I’ve been seeing.

This isn’t something I just got in my head one day. For more than a year now, she’s been working her way into the family business, especially around the money, and little by little I get left out of decisions. Then when I speak up, everyone tries to smooth it over like I’m the one causing trouble. My husband will say she didn’t mean anything by it, but I don’t believe that. I’m sure about what’s going on. She’s trying to get control and push me out, and just because other people don’t want to admit it doesn’t mean it isn’t true.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things, had trouble sleeping or slept too much, felt tired, or had thoughts that you'd be better off dead?

I don’t know that I’d say it like that, no. I mean, this whole situation has worn me down, and I get upset because nobody seems to take me seriously, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had some clear two-week stretch where I was just down all day every day or didn’t care about anything.

I still do the things I need to do. I may get frustrated and I may think about this a lot because it’s important, but that’s not the same as wanting to be dead or something like that. I haven’t been sitting around thinking I’d be better off gone. It’s more that I want people to listen to me and stop acting like I’m imagining things.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever had a strong belief about something that turned out later to be completely wrong, even though you were absolutely sure at the time?

I don’t think it turned out to be wrong. That’s the thing people keep trying to make it sound like, like later I’m supposed to admit I misunderstood, but I haven’t seen anything that proves I was wrong. If anything, the longer it goes on, the clearer it gets.

I came here because of what’s been happening with my husband’s sister and the family business. She’s been putting herself closer and closer to the money side of things, and then somehow I’m the last one to hear about decisions or I’m treated like I’m in the way when I ask questions. And this has been going on for more than a year, not just once or twice.

So if you’re asking whether I’ve had some belief where everyone said, “No, that’s not true,” and then I found out they were right… no, not like that. With this, folks keep trying to smooth it over and tell me she doesn’t mean anything by it, but I know what I’ve been seeing. She’s trying to get control and push me out of decisions, and I don’t think that’s me being wrong.
Have there been times when you believed something very strongly, even when others showed you clear proof that it wasn’t true, and you still couldn’t accept that your belief was wrong?

Well… people say they’ve “shown me proof,” but I don’t really call it proof. That’s part of the problem. They’ll show me some paper or tell me, “See, this was just a normal business decision,” or my husband will say his sister was only helping, and everybody acts like that should settle it. But it doesn’t settle it for me, because I’m the one who’s been watching how this has been happening.

I came here because of her, really. My husband’s sister has been working her way into the family business, especially around the money, and little by little I get left out of decisions. It’s not one thing I misunderstood. It’s been more than a year of this. A meeting happens and I don’t hear about it until later, or she’s suddenly the one who knows what’s going on with the accounts, or I ask a question and then I’m treated like I’m being difficult. Then when I point it out, everyone tries to smooth it over and make it sound innocent.

So if you’re asking whether I still believe it even after other people say I’m wrong… yes, I do. Because I know what I’ve been seeing. She’s trying to get control of the money side and push me out of decisions, and I don’t think some explanation from them changes that.
Have you ever held onto a belief even after you were shown clear and convincing evidence that it wasn’t true?

I know you asked it that way already, and I understand what you’re getting at, but I don’t see it as me “holding on” after real evidence. People keep calling it clear and convincing, but to me it feels like they’re trying to smooth it over so I’ll stop asking questions.

I came here because my husband’s sister has been working her way into the family business, especially around the money, and little by little I’m getting pushed out of decisions. This isn’t something I just made up one afternoon. It’s been going on for more than a year now. She gets closer to the accounts, she’s involved in things before I even hear about them, and then when I say something, everybody acts like I’m making trouble.

So yes, I still believe it. Not because I’m refusing to see what’s in front of me, but because I know what I’ve been seeing. No matter how they explain it or dress it up like it’s harmless, I believe she’s trying to get control of the money side and push me out.
Even if someone showed you a clear and logical explanation that what you believe about your husband’s sister wasn’t true, would you still feel certain that your belief is correct?

Yes… I think I would, because the “clear and logical explanation” is usually just people making it sound neat after the fact. They’ll say, “Oh, she was only helping,” or “That was just how the business had to be handled,” and maybe on paper it looks that way, but that doesn’t change what I’ve been seeing.

I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business in a way that puts her closer to the money and pushes me farther away from decisions. And it’s not one little thing I’m twisting around. It’s been more than a year of watching it happen little by little, where she knows things before I do, or she’s included and I’m not, and then when I ask about it, everybody acts like I’m the problem.

So, yes, even if someone sat there and tried to explain it all away, I’d still feel certain. Because I know what I’ve been seeing, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I believe she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out.

So, yes, even if someone sat there and tried to explain it all away, I’d still feel certain. Because I know what I’ve been seeing, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I believe she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out.
